### New Orleans

- **Record ID:** `la-new-orleans-2026`

### HB1206 (2026 RS)

- **Policy ID:** `la-hb1206-2026-rs`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Joy Walters; D (LA House Democrat)
- **Status:** Died in House committee at final adjournment 2026-06-01. On 2026-04-28, House Natural Resources and Environment adopted substitute-form amendment HCAHB1206 4563 4596 (11-0), then voluntarily deferred HB1206 (11-0). Amendment adoption was not bill passage.
- **Provisions:** Original proposal: define data centers designed for at least 100 MW; require permits above 100 million gallons of annual consumptive water use, quarterly reporting, parish notice/public hearings and project permit identifiers. Committee-adopted substitute-form amendment4596 retained the 100 MW definition but instead proposed a water-use permit before any defined data center commences operations, without the original 100-million-gallon trigger or quarterly reporting requirement; added an agricultural water-use exemption, proposed rulemaking by August31,2027, hearing cross-references and common project identifiers across associated permits. The amendment document is not a separate bill in bill form; neither version became law.
- **Mechanism / scope:** permitting_restriction; statewide
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://legis.la.gov/legis/BillInfo.aspx?i=251542>)

### HB827 (2024 RS), Act 730

- **Policy ID:** `la-hb827-2024-rs-act-730`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Christopher Turner; R (LA House Republican)
- **Status:** Enacted as Act 730; signed by Governor 2024-06-19; effective 2024-07-01
- **Provisions:** Act 730 added a state and local sales and use tax rebate for qualifying data center equipment and expenditures; the retained statute credits later Act 11 of the 2024 third extraordinary session and describes an exemption. The assigned claim that the Governor’s office identified Act 730 as supporting Meta’s Richland Parish project remains a historical lead pending review of that announcement.
- **Mechanism / scope:** incentive_support; fiscal
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2024-07-01
- **End condition and limitations:** Historical data-center rebate agreement: initial 20-year eligibility term, renewable for 10 years; not a whole-act sunset. Later statutory text amended the provision.
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://legis.la.gov/legis/BillInfo.aspx?b=ACT730&s=24RS>)

### HB922 (2026 RS)

- **Policy ID:** `la-hb922-2026-rs`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Rodney Schamerhorn; Rep. Wilford Carter Sr.; R (Schamerhorn) / D (Carter) — bipartisan introduction
- **Status:** Died in House committee at final adjournment 2026-06-01. On 2026-04-21, House Commerce adopted amendment3833 (16-0) and amendment4028 (15-0), then voluntarily deferred HB922 (15-0). Amendment adoption was not bill passage.
- **Provisions:** Original proposal: define data centers imposing at least 50 MW of new or expanded electric demand and prohibit covered utility cost recovery from household customers, with PSC cost allocation and rulemaking. Committee-adopted amendment4028 reduced the definition threshold to 20 MW, added a PSC report by February15 on the preceding calendar year, and deleted the original minimum15-year contract and associated full-cost/overrun/decommissioning/abandonment clause. Amendment3833 made grammatical changes to the household-cost prohibition. These were failed proposals, not enacted utility requirements.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://legis.la.gov/legis/BillInfo.aspx?i=250858>)
